name: cinnabar_lacquer
what: Vermilion lacquer (朱漆): alpha-HgS (cinnabar / vermilion) pigment in cured Asian lacquer (urushi, 大漆), polished; with the black lacquer that carved lacquer builds with it (剔红 marker lines, 剔犀 bands). Substance only: the carving, the layer stack are crafts/carving; wear, haze, scratches, cracks and grime are crafts/aging.

tags.M: measured: a measurement reported in the source, or measured by us on a photo or a render
tags.I: looked up: a value a source gives but did not measure itself (handbook, catalogue, review)
tags.D: derived: computed from other values, the method written out
tags.F: fitted: tuned until the render matches the reference; an output of the material card, with what it matched and how
tags.A: assumed: our assumption or a placeholder

model: an opaque body (Lambertian, reflectance R(lambda) per lacquer) under a smooth-to-glossy dielectric interface of the lacquer polymer (GGX). The interface is where the gloss and the Saunderson deepening of the colour come from. Until the shared 'clear layer over a diffuse body' lands in the adapter, the card builds it as geometry: a dielectric sheet (the surface) and the body a little below it (coat_gap_mm), both rendered by the existing adapter branches.

eta.source: refractive index of raw lacquer 1.52, black lacquer 1.55 (保存科学 No. 45, 2006, Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties, pp. 251-; table of lacquer properties; https://www.tobunken.go.jp/ccr/pdf/45/04524.pdf). The paper's Japanese text did not extract cleanly; the numbers and row labels did. Taken as constant over the visible (no dispersion data) [A]

ggx_alpha_fresh.source: 60-degree gloss of fresh Chinese lacquer films 88.96-90.96 GU (BYK micro-TRI-gloss, 5 points; Hou et al. 2025, Polymers 17:1481, Table 2, doi 10.3390/polym17111481) -> tools/gloss.py with n 1.52. Ra 0.122-0.138 um (MarSurf, same table). A new film, not a centuries-old carved surface

ggx_alpha.source: the new, polished surface = ggx_alpha_fresh. An old piece's satin is not the material's: it comes from the processes on its surface, by their parameters (crafts/weathering skin_alpha, crafts/wear rubbed_alpha and scratches; docs/crafts/surface.md), fitted on the card to the photo's state (state_cma1918933.json)

coat_gap_mm.source: the binder-rich skin above the pigment; only a geometric stand-in for 'the interface lies on the body'. No absorption in it (the binder's absorption is inside the body reflectance). Up to the NGV mean layer 0.059 mm

body.what: body reflectance of each lacquer (no interface): a family the craft indexes by layer (familymap). Spectra in 'derived', made by derive.py

red.source: Reichert et al. 2025, Anal. Bioanal. Chem. 417:4351-4372, doi 10.1007/s00216-025-05948-3; data doi 10.6084/m9.figshare.28639103 (CC BY 4.0): HSI mean spectrum of cinnabar in gum arabic on paper (06A, VNIR, 5 nm) [M], less the flat reading of grape-seed black in the same binder on the same paper (15A, 0.16) [A: that the black's reading is the flat part common to the paints; derive.py]. The pigment is a reference cinnabar for manuscript paints, not the pigment of any lacquer piece. Used as the body under the lacquer's interface as it is [A: a lean matte paint has no smooth interface of its own]

scattering_S_per_mm.source: the Kubelka-Munk scattering coefficient of the pigment in the lacquer: the binder adds K_b/S to the paint's K/S (body = KM R_inf). Not measured for any red lacquer; a recipe of 10 wt% cinnabar to lacquer (Coatings 2025, 15:1229, methods [I]) is ~1.6 vol% (densities 8.1 and ~1.3 [A]) and would give tens per mm for micron grains [D, rough]. Fitted on the card to the photo's colour (G/R, B/R over the lacquer); null = no binder absorption. Fitted value 150 /mm on the overview (k350 lights, process state of the CMA dish): with the binder at 60 /mm the body is too dark and brown (over-backdrop R 0.41 by the 1-D estimate, the c1 card 'jujube red'), without it (S = null) too bright (R 1.23 over the backdrop against the photo's 0.85, glossy frame); 150 gives R 0.85 on the glossy frame and 0.90 with the fitted satin. 100 gives 0.80, 250 gives 1.04

black.source: black lacquer (urushi with carbon or iron black): the body is near black; the gloss comes from the interface. Not measured

pigment.what: facts about the pigment that are not parameters of the model (no number was found that would make them one)
pigment.band_gap: alpha-HgS: experimental gap ~2.25 eV (~550 nm) as reported by Cardona et al. 2010 (PRB 82:085210), citing Zallen 1967 [I: secondary report]; the measured paints rise at ~570 nm and inflect at ~600 nm (Fioretti et al. 2023, Heritage 6:1567, Table 5) [M]; derived.cinnabar inflects at the same place
pigment.particle_size: coarse grades (63-100 um) bluish red, extra fine (<20 um) more orange red, in one Hunan series (Elert & Cardell 2019, Spectrochim. Acta A 216:236) [M, qualitative]; not a general size-to-colour law (their fine Almaden pigment stayed bluish). No parameter
pigment.concentration: no measured pigment fraction of a historical Chinese red lacquer was found (research carved-lacquer). A modern experimental cinnabar lacquer used 10 wt% pigment to lacquer (Coatings 2025, 15(10):1229, doi 10.3390/coatings15101229) [I]. The body is taken as opaque (R_inf): the NGV fragment has >=17 red layers in ~1 mm [M], and the binder alone absorbs 8-60 /mm [D, binder]
pigment.darkening: photo-darkening (metallic Hg, Elert et al. 2021; chlorine, Pisu et al. 2023) is not modelled

derived.what: made by derive.py from the Reichert 2025 CSVs (ref/, not in git): (R_paint - R_black) / (1 - R_black), sampled 400-780 nm at 10 nm [D]

binder.what: the cured lacquer polymer's own absorption, from the visible transmission of a clear (unpigmented) urushi film

transmission_30um_pct.source: Oyabu & Asami 1987, 'Effects of curing condition on transparency of urushi films', J. Jpn. Soc. Colour Mater. (色材) 60(2):94-99, doi 10.4011/shikizai1937.60.94, Fig. 6: sugurome-urushi cured 24 h at 20 C / 80% RH, then 90 days under north-window daylight; transmission corrected by the authors to 30 um (Lambert's law), Shimadzu UV-350A, 380-780 nm. The 90-day curve (the most aged of the three; a centuries-old surface may differ further) read off the scanned figure by us column by column (tick-calibrated, about +-1% T); below 430 nm the curve is at 0. File: ref/carved_lacquer/oyabu1987/

absorption_per_mm.method: a = -ln(T / T0) / 0.030 mm with T0 = (1 - R)^2, R = ((n - 1)/(n + 1))^2 for n 1.52 (two film faces, multiple reflections neglected): a(600 nm) ~ 20 /mm, a(500) ~ 58 /mm, a(700) ~ 8 /mm. Below 430 nm held at the 430 nm value (the figure reads 0 there; the sensor x key weight below 430 nm is ~1%)

km_K_over_a.source: Kubelka-Munk K = 2 x the absorption coefficient for diffuse light (the usual relation, e.g. Kortuem 1969)
